title: Design System: Bearden High Robotics Club

display.purpose: Hero statement only. Archivo 800 at width 125.

headline.purpose: Section titles, short sentences ending in a period.

spec-term.purpose: Verbs in the About spec list, paired with a maroon line icon.

title.purpose: Subsection heads; the 700/width-110 voice is shared by buttons and table captions.

lede.purpose: Intro paragraphs in Graphite, 34ch in the hero, 52ch in sections.

label.purpose: Mono with tabular numerals for part numbers, quantities, captions, title-block values, and TBD marks.

lines.name: stroke-default
lines.purpose: Every edge in drawings and icons; frame rules of tables, spec list, title block.

lines.name: stroke-thin
lines.purpose: Thin detail, leader lines, center lines.

lines.name: rule-inner
lines.purpose: Row and cell dividers inside ruled blocks; grid lines.

lines.name: dash-center
lines.purpose: Center lines in the drawing (5 2 1 2 at icon scale).

lines.name: dash-guide
lines.purpose: Assembly guides from a part to its home position.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Color, background, and opacity state changes at 0.2-0.3s.

motion.name: ease-assembly
motion.purpose: Scroll-linked travel of each part along its guide into place.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: transitions none; hero static and assembled

components.css: .ds-bom { width: 420px; border-collapse: collapse; background: #eef1f4; border: 1.5px solid #1f2328; font-family: 'Archivo', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; line-height: 1.3; color: #1f2328; } .ds-bom caption { padding: 6px 10px; border: 1.5px solid #1f2328; border-bottom: 0; background: #eef1f4; font-weight: 700; font-variation-settings: 'wdth' 110; text-align: left; } .ds-bom th, .ds-bom td { padding: 4px 10px; border-top: 1px solid #c9d0d8; text-align: left; } .ds-bom th { font-weight: 600; color: #545b64; } .ds-mono { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-bom tr { transition: background-color 0.25s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), color 0.25s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-bom tr[data-state='active'] { background: #f1e3e5; color: #7a1f2e; } .ds-bom tr[data-state='placed'] { color: #545b64; } .ds-check { width: 28px; } .ds-bom tr[data-state='placed'] .ds-check::after { content: ''; display: block; width: 5px; height: 10px; margin-left: 4px; border: solid #545b64; border-width: 0 2px 2px 0; transform: rotate(45deg); }

narrative.overview:
The whole site is a build manual a student could actually follow: cool-gray blueprint paper ruled with a fine grid, ink-gray technical line art, and Bearden maroon used as drafting-pen ink for whatever matters right now (the part being placed, the call to action, the Join field). Every device comes from engineering drawings: balloons with leader lines, dashed assembly guides, center lines, dimension lines with arrowheads, a parts list, and a title block that closes the page. Nothing is rendered, lit, or glowing. The robot is a line drawing, and the content sits on the sheet like annotations.

The page is light, calm, and deliberately sparse. Type is wide, heavy Archivo for anything spoken aloud and JetBrains Mono only for things you would read off a drawing (part numbers, quantities, step captions, placeholders). Depth comes from line weight and ink value, never from shadows. The only full color field on the page is the maroon Join section, which makes the single action unmissable.

The rejected default is the robotics category look: dark hero, glowing robot render, icon-card grids. Honesty is part of the look too: anything the club has not decided yet is drawn as a dashed, monospaced "TBD" mark, the way an unfinished drawing marks a value still to be confirmed.
keyCharacteristics: Light blueprint paper with a two-level grid (24px minor, 120px major) behind every section.
Line art at a single weight (1.5px, non-scaling) with 0.75px for thin, center, and leader lines.
Maroon is a state and an action color, never decoration.
Square, ruled forms: 1px and 1.5px rules, 2px corner at most on interface chrome.
Wide Archivo headings; monospace only for drawing data.
Motion is assembly: parts travel along their guides as you scroll; everything else is a short color fade.

rules.name: The Pen-Ink Rule
rules.body: Maroon marks what is active or actionable: the part being placed, the thing to click, the Join field. If an element is neither, it is drawn in ink or graphite.

rules.name: The Lines-Only Gray Rule
rules.body: Construction Gray (about 3.4:1 on paper) is for strokes and rules, never for text. Secondary text uses Graphite, which clears 4.5:1.

rules.name: The Drawing-Data Rule
rules.body: Monospace is reserved for values you would read off a drawing: numbers, part codes, captions, TBD marks. Headings, buttons, and prose are never set in mono (the placeholder button is the one exception, because its label is itself a TBD mark).

rules.name: The Wide-For-Weight Rule
rules.body: Weight and width rise together. Headings use width 110–125; body text stays at default width.

rules.name: The Drafted-Depth Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy comes from line weight, dash pattern, and ink value. A shadow, glow, or blur on this sheet is a foreign object.

dos: Do keep the two-level blueprint grid (24px minor, 120px major, 1px rules) behind the page; it is part of the world.
Do fill drawn parts, tables, and the title block with Blueprint Paper so they sit on top of the grid.
Do draw new illustrations and icons in the robot's stroke language: 1.5px round-joined strokes, 0.75px for thin and center lines, maroon only for the active element.
Do mark every undecided fact with the dashed mono TBD mark instead of inventing a value.
Do use the out-expo curve (cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)) at 0.2–0.3s for color and opacity state changes, and drop all transitions under reduced motion.
Do keep text at Graphite or darker on paper, and On Maroon Soft or lighter on maroon.
donts: Don't use shadows, glows, blur, or soft tonal gradients; the grid's 1px rules are the only gradient-built thing on the page.
Don't set text in Construction Gray.
Don't use maroon for decoration or for more than one full-bleed field per page.
Don't round interface chrome beyond 2px or wrap content in cards; group with rules and ruled tables as a drawing would.
Don't use dashed lines casually; dashes mean an assembly guide, a hidden line, or a placeholder.
Don't set prose, headings, or buttons in monospace (the placeholder button excepted).
